_why_this_exists_before_the_review_does: AUT-PROP-006. This record is written as the seat's FIRST act, so a seat that dies leaves evidence that it looked rather than nothing at all. It is EMPTY and says so: publish_bar.clause_1_hardening_converged REFUSES any round with an open record at the commit it is grading, because an unfinished look must never be counted as a clean one.
central_claim: Re-deriving the real in-frame EWSR1::NR4A3 junctions from the transcript model grades all 27 declared exon pairs, emits 5 junctions and 11 distinct predicted MHC-I binders (4 strong), none pan-EMC, and the HLA population coverage that follows is small (8.51% on the public e7::e3 junction, 27.4% pooled over all strong-binder alleles) - so a fusion-exclusive EMC immunotherapy is personalised by necessity and its public-junction addressable fraction is under a tenth of patients. Every one of those figures re-derives exactly from research/modalities/fusion-breakpoint-neoantigens.json and research/modalities/hla-coverage.json, so the central claim is supported.

blockers.quote: 5. **Coverage floor and inequity.** Population coverage is partial (~30% public junction, ~58% all strong alleles, ~16% both-arms floor) and varies ~36-79% by region; a fixed allele panel tuned on one population under-serves others. The class-II / both-arms figures are floors over a 3-allele DR test panel
blockers.why: All five figures in this sentence are the RETRACTED pre-2026-08-07 values, printed as live text with no supersession marker - and this paper's own abstract lists exactly these as withdrawn (its supersession box names '~30% / 29.7% e7::e3 coverage on A*11:01 + B*08:01', '~58% / 58.0% all-strong', '36% Sub-Saharan Africa to 79% Northern Europe', 'the ~16% both-arms floor'). Against research/modalities/hla-coverage.json at the pin: global.coverage_e7e3_public = 0.0851 (8.5%, not ~30%); global.coverage_any_strong_binder_allele = 0.2737 (27.4%, not ~58%); global.coverage_cd8_and_cd4_combined = 0.0178 (1.8%, not ~16% - a nine-fold overstatement); the regional spread in `regions` for coverage_any_strong_binder_allele runs 0.0137 (Melanesia) to 0.6043 (Northern Europe), i.e. 1.4-60%, and nothing in that file is 36% or 79%. The '3-allele DR test panel' is also wrong: hla-coverage.json `_class_ii_note` records a 23-allele DR/DP/DQ panel and patient-cd4-demo.json has n_alleles_screened = 23 with alleles_without_a_model = []. §3 of this same paper states the corrected figures (8.51%, 27.4%, 1.4%-60%) and states explicitly that 'The panel is no longer three alleles', so §6.5 also contradicts the paper's own body. A reader who reaches the Limitations section - the section a sceptical reader reads first - is told the route reaches roughly three times as many patients on a public junction, twice as many overall, and nine times as many on both arms, as the committed artifact supports.
blockers.fix: Replace item 5 with: '**Coverage floor and inequity.** Population coverage is partial - 8.5% for the public e7::e3 junction, 27.4% pooled over all strong-binder alleles (§3) - and varies from 1.4% (Melanesia) to 60% (Northern Europe) for any strong binder; a fixed allele panel tuned on one population under-serves others. The class-II and both-arms figures are floors over the 23-allele DR/DP/DQ test panel recorded in `hla-coverage.json`, and the coverage formula assumes cross-locus independence (it ignores linkage disequilibrium between HLA class-I and DRB1 loci).'

blockers.quote: **Personalised is necessary and acceptable:** §2 shows there is no off-the-shelf pan-EMC epitope (necessity), while §3 shows the presenting alleles are among the most common worldwide, so many patients carry >=1 (acceptability).
blockers.why: This restates as live text the clause the paper's own abstract records as withdrawn: the supersession box in the abstract names 'the clause "**acceptable** (the platforms already exist in humans, and many patients carry a presenting allele)" - which the recomputed coverage no longer supports as written.' §3 does not show that many patients carry a presenting allele: research/modalities/hla-coverage.json global.coverage_any_strong_binder_allele = 0.2737, and §3 itself draws the complement - 'even the full multi-allele panel leaves ~73% with no predicted strong-binding class-I allele'. So §4(a) cites §3 for the opposite of what §3 computes.
blockers.fix: Replace the sentence with: '**Personalised is necessary, and its reach is bounded:** §2 shows there is no off-the-shelf pan-EMC epitope (necessity), while §3 shows that even pooling every strong-binder allele reaches only 27.4% of patients, so a vaccine built on these predicted binders leaves roughly three-quarters of patients with no predicted presenting class-I allele.'

blockers.quote: Across all three, the fusion-exclusivity is the shared selling point: the target peptide is absent from the normal proteome, so on-target/off-tumour toxicity against wild-type NR4A3- or EWSR1-expressing tissue is, in principle, not possible - the failure mode that haunts shared-antigen TCR therapies.
blockers.why: The paper's own abstract states the opposite of the premise and disclaims the conclusion: 'the novelty test behind this compares the junction peptides against those two parent proteins only (`fusion_breakpoints.emit_junction`'s novelty filter), never against the human proteome, and no safety claim is made or supported.' §1 repeats it ('it spares wild-type NR4A3 and EWSR1 at the sequence level - NOT every normal cell, which no test here has assessed'). The artifact agrees: research/modalities/fusion-neoantigen-retraction.json breakpoint_artifact.what_was_checked records only 'every peptide the artifact asserts is absent from BOTH parent proteins', and its `what_this_does_NOT_establish` field states 'No efficacy, safety, tolerability or clinical claim is made or implied.' 'Absent from the normal proteome' is a proteome-wide selectivity claim that no committed artifact tests, and 'toxicity ... is, in principle, not possible' is a safety claim - both forbidden by the language discipline this paper is held to. systems/AUDIT-2026-08-06-routes.md line 492 already flagged the earlier wording of this same sentence ('cannot, in principle, harm any normal cell') for exactly this reason; the rewording did not remove the claim.
blockers.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Across all three, the fusion-exclusivity is the shared premise: the junction peptides are absent from both parent proteins, EWSR1 and NR4A3, so a response against them does not target the wild-type receptor at the sequence level. That novelty test was run against those two proteins only and never against the human proteome, so it bounds nothing about off-tumour toxicity, which remains untested here.'

p1s.what: No committed test binds any number in this manuscript to the artifact that produces it. `git grep -l 'fusion-junction-neoantigen-paper'` over research/manuscripts/tests, research/modalities/tests and scripts at the pin returns nothing, and the paper is absent from research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json (which lists its sibling emc-vaccine-development-path.md four times, and that sibling IS guarded by research/manuscripts/tests/test_vaccine_path_numbers.py). So the paper's 27 / 5 / 11 / 4 / 38 counts, its whole binder table (11 rows of affinity and presentation percentile), its 8.51% and 27.4% coverages with their CIs, and its regional figures are all free-typed prose that would not go red if hla-coverage.json or fusion-breakpoint-neoantigens.json were regenerated with different values.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: Every one of those numbers re-derives correctly against the artifacts at this pin - I checked all of them - so the text is right today. But B1 is precisely this gap having already fired once: the §3 numbers were updated when the seam was corrected and the §6.5 copies were not, and nothing caught it for the ~3.5 weeks since. A guard that asserted every percentage in this paper against hla-coverage.json would have made B1 impossible.

p1s.what: Inside the retained-superseded blockquote, the closing sentence asserts in the present tense: 'The mechanical point that a durable vaccine needs both arms, and that the class-II screen tested only a 3-allele DR test panel (DRB1*15:01/03:01/07:01) and so gives a **floor**, is unaffected.' Two sentences above it, in the same blockquote, the 2026-08-28 correction says 'The panel is no longer three alleles - every declared allele in a DR/DP/DQ panel several times that size was scored, and `alleles_without_a_model` is empty.' patient-cd4-demo.json confirms n_alleles_screened = 23. So the block's 'is unaffected' clause contradicts the block's own correction.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: It sits inside a blockquote whose header states 'The paragraph below describes the state before that rebuild and is retained as the record of it', so a careful reader can read it as historical. The live, unqualified version of the same error is §6.5 and is filed as B1. But 'is unaffected' is a present-tense currency claim, and the next edit that trims a superseded block would carry it forward as live text.

p1s.what: The paper deliberately holds no copy of the class-II or both-arms numbers, pointing instead at emc-vaccine-development-path.md §B4 as their 'one home'. That is correct under one-fact-one-place, but it means nothing in this paper's own text is checkable against hla-coverage.json's `coverage_cd4_classii` (0.0649) and `coverage_cd8_and_cd4_combined` (0.0178), and the pointer is to a file that does not ship with this paper (the outgoing set is this markdown file alone).
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: Omitting a number is not stating a wrong one, and §3 characterises the direction honestly ('several-fold SMALLER than the retired figure', which 6.49% vs 28.4% supports). A reader of the shipped artifact simply cannot see the figure, which is a completeness problem rather than a false statement.

p2s.what: The linkage-disequilibrium illustration names 'the A1-B8-DR3 ancestral haplotype links B*08:01 and DRB1*03:01'. Neither allele is in any set this paper now uses: hla-coverage.json's class-I sets are [HLA-B*15:01] and [HLA-A*01:01, HLA-B*07:02, HLA-B*15:01], and class_ii_cd4_helper_alleles is [DRB1*14:01]. The general point about cross-locus independence is sound, but the example is a leftover from the retracted allele set and will read to a reviewer as evidence the section was not updated.

The `title:` field is truncated mid-word - 'a fusion-exclusive immunot' - while the H1 on the next line carries the full title. The truncation has already propagated: systems/views/L2-rt-junction-neoantigen.md line 99, systems/views/L2-rt-tcr-immtac.md line 89 and systems/views/L3-publications.md all render the paper's name ending in 'immunot'. Since this markdown file IS the outgoing artifact, the broken title ships with it.

Repository tooling (not the outgoing set) still describes fusion-breakpoint-neoantigens.json as carrying '7 in-frame junctions'. The committed artifact has n_inframe_junctions = 5. target-route-options.md marks it as superseded-retained; the census JSON and the two scripts state it flat. This is out of scope as a blocker per the brief and is recorded only so the stale string is findable.

The paper names the predictor 'MHCflurry-2.0' throughout and cites O'Donnell 2020. The artifact's `_predictor` block records tool 'MHCflurry', version '2.1.4', models_release '2.2.0'. The method name matches the citation, so this is not a wrong statement, but the exact tool and model-release version a reader would need to reproduce the table appears nowhere in the paper.
